newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty tests upside as foreigners buy bills.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty tests upside as foreigners buy bills.

text.p: The zloty inched up against the basket of currencies in early Monday trade amid light foreign investor entry into Polish treasuries, dealers said.
"Foreigners may be selling dollars, which is pushing the zloty over resistance at 1.5 percent from the parity rate," said Maciej Grabosz, forex dealer at Bank Zachodni SA.
At 0835 GMT the zloty was at 1.53/1.48 percent from parity, against 1.50/1.44 percent at opening.
"There are some (currency) selling orders and trade seems to be nervous as banks test the resistance border," said Marcin Trzykowski, forex dealer at Pekao SA.
The zloty was at 3.2410/22 to the dollar up from opening's 3.2450/70 and at 1.8690/06 to the mark, down from 1.8675/85.

Dealers said foreign investors may be buying zlotys for T-bills which they hope to aquire at Monday's 1.4 billion zloty primary auction. Yields are expected to rise as the finance ministry is seen having problems with budget financing.
On the money market one-day rates slipped after the central bank decided not to stage any open market operations on Monday.
Overnight rates eased to 21.80/22.00 percent from opening's 22.05/22.15 and tomorrow/next to 21.95/21.15 percent from Friday's 22.05/22.30. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
